chunks: And I desired naught but reform what I am able to (do); and my guidance is not but with Allāh; On Him (alone) do I rely, and unto Him (alone) do I turn.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali mean when he said 'I desired naught but reform'?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs this verse to counter Muawiya’s accusations of ambition, framing his governance as a duty of *Islah* (reform) rather than personal aggrandizement. This aligns with the Shia understanding of the Imamate as a divine trust, where authority is exercised with humility and ultimate reliance on God, distinguishing the Ahl al-Bayt’s leadership from the political opportunism of the Umayyads.
